speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I understand you have chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To narrow this down, have you noticed any blood in your urine, fever, or pain during urination? Also, how many times a day are you currently voiding?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome. The combination of chronic suprapubic pain relieved by voiding, nighttime frequency, and recent dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female is classic for this condition; the absence of urinary tract infection symptoms and the failure of NSAIDs to resolve it further supports this.
